newsitem.title: UK: GPT wins 50 mln stg Belgian order.
newsitem.headline: GPT wins 50 mln stg Belgian order.

text.p: GPT, the UK telecoms manufacturer owned by electronics giants General Electric Co Plc and Siemens AG, said on Wednesday its global STEP alliance had won a 50 million stg equipment order from Belgian national carrier Belgacom.

STEP -- GPT's partnership with Germany's Siemens -- won three-year sole supplier contracts for new transmission and network access equipment through its Siemens Atea subsidiary which operates in Belgium.

Belgacom needs to upgrade its national and regional transmission networks ahead of the opening of continental Europe's telecoms markets in 1998. It also wants to pursue opportunities outside its national borders.

GPT and Siemens' expansion has been partly built on the success of its Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SDH) technology -- which is a key component of high capacity information systems such as the Internet.

The technology, which already links China with western Europe in a 27,000 km high-speed transmission network, is capable of carrying up to 48 broadcast-quality television channels or 30,000 simultaneous telephone calls.

Over the next three years, Siemens Atea will supply Belgacom with SDH products and equipment for both its core and access networks. The venture will also supply spares, maintenance and management software upgrades for at least the next 10 years.

"The orders account for around 95 percent of Belgacom's SDH equipment requirements and are a clear demonstration of both the technical leadership of our SDH technology and the strength of the STEP alliance between GPT and Siemens," GPT said in a statement.

GPT says its Siemens alliance is a world market leader in SDH, accounting for over 30 percent of sales in the global SDH market, which is estimated to grow to 2.0 billion stg from around 1.1 billion by the year 2000.

GEC said on Tuesday it was considering "repositioning" its GPT joint venture but had decided against selling it to Siemens because of the high-growth nature of the telecoms market. It is monitoring the business.
